title: Contract-approval notices: how long after the approval they were filed
question: When an elected officer or the Board approves a contract of $100,000 or more, a notice naming the contractor’s officers must reach the Ethics Commission within five business days. How often does it?
finding: Of 7,047 original notices for approvals dated from January 2019 to 2026-11-06, 2,975 (42.2%) were filed more than five business days after the approval date typed on them. The Mayor’s notices account for most: 2,497 of 3,830 (65.2%) were late, 695 by more than 90 days and 186 by more than a year, with a typical (median) gap of 13 days. The Board of Supervisors’ notices, filed by its Clerk, were late in 210 of 2,513 cases (8.4%). All 169 notices for Retirement Board approvals were late, typically by 71 days.
how: Each notice is one filing with two dates on it: the approval date and the day it was signed (DocuSign form) or filed (the 2026 system). The form’s own instruction is the yardstick: the officer “must file this form with the Ethics Commission within five business days of approval” (SFEC Form 126(f)4 v.12.7.18). Business days are weekdays; public holidays are not removed, so a notice counted one or two days late over a holiday week may have been on time, which is why the counts over 30, 90 and 365 calendar days are printed too. Amendments (382), notices with a date missing (18) and notices whose two dates cannot both be right (11: an approval year before 2015, or a gap of more than 1,500 days or less than minus 400) are left out. A notice signed before its approval date counts as on time and is shown in its own column.
limits: The approval date is whatever the filer typed. For a contract the Board approves, the Mayor’s notice may give the Board’s vote or the Mayor’s signature a few days later; that can move a notice by days, not by months. A late notice is a filing lapse by a City office, not conduct by the contractor, and many are batches caught up on one day. The everyday reasons are staff turnover, grant agreements signed in bulk each autumn, and a change of filing system in 2026. No file on disk says whether the Ethics Commission has reviewed lateness.
